scope: Six non-MSA/non-MERC VQA bilinear readout adaptations; literature and official implementation inspection only. No source-paper reproduction or cfg84 performance claim.
provenance_policy: Primary PDFs and actual author-owned code files were read. URLs below are sources, not copied implementation. Small dimensions and cfg84 integration are proposed adaptations.

common_adaptation.input: Existing Local L[N,D_L] and four already-computed contexts E=[Base,GapA,GapT,GapV], with authoritative active/history/padding masks. No new memory scan, state write, completion or JEPA.
common_adaptation.pooling: For non-BAN candidates, use the active mean of the four typed history/context tokens as C. Do not infer context validity from zero-valued features. Sanitize inactive tokens with where before operations, and reapply masks after biased projections.
common_adaptation.integration: Return interaction delta in a small latent space, then use the common output projection into original cfg84 Flat pre-normalization width1600. This residual wrapper and its zero initialization are cfg84 choices, not claims about the source architectures.
common_adaptation.masks: All-inactive context rows return exactly zero and remain finite. BAN masks attention logits using explicit active flags and handles all-masked rows separately. No future/history trajectory access is introduced.
common_adaptation.training: Original cfg84 objective, optimizer, missing-mask protocol and checkpoint selection stay unchanged. All original and new trainable parameters retain gradients. Proposed fixed dimensions are initial choices, not literature-tuned cfg84 hyperparameters.

methods.title: Hadamard Product for Low-rank Bilinear Pooling
methods.paperEvidence: Sections2–3, Eq.(3) and Eq.(5): projected Hadamard product followed by output projection; Section4 is the larger attention architecture.

codeFiles.verified: Tanh-projected question and visual embeddings, CMulTable for elementwise fusion, final Linear projection.

license.note: Manual LICENSE inspection and README identify BSD3; GitHub API reports NOASSERTION. README also carries a patent-pending notice; no legal conclusion inferred.

algorithm.dimensions: L[N,D_L], C[N,D_C]; U:D_L→r, V:D_C→r, P:r→D; proposed r=D=128.
algorithm.pytorch_plan: Two Linear projections, tanh, elementwise product, output Linear. This extracts the pooling operator; it omits the VQA attention and classifiers.

methods.distinctness: One learned joint rank space, without factor-group sum, rank-constrained second-stage Tucker core, blockwise core, fixed sketch or evidence attention.
caveats: A learned residual around existing Flat is our wrapper; the final MLB VQA model itself is described as no-shortcut.
Learned projections may change signs/scales; there is no inherited guarantee of better cfg84 W-F1.

methods.title: Multi-modal Factorized Bilinear Pooling with Co-Attention Learning for Visual Question Answering
methods.paperEvidence: Section3, Eq.(4), Fig.1: projected product to k*o, nonoverlapping sum pooling of k factors, signed-square-root and L2 normalization.

codeFiles.verified: Original Caffe construction projects both inputs, multiplies, reshapes to output-by-factor, sum pools, then SignedSqrt and L2Normalize.
Original repo explicitly links OpenVQA as its maintained implementation. First-stage path expands K*O, multiplies, AvgPool1d*K, signed sqrt, and normalization.

successor.id: Apache-2.0 at repository root; MIT named in file header

license.note: Original repo has no detected license file; successor root/file license labels conflict. Use a fresh formula-based implementation rather than copying either source.

algorithm.pytorch_plan: Product, reshape N,o,k and sum over k. The implementation uses continuous q/sqrt(abs(q)+1e-8) and L2 epsilon1e-8 to keep gradients finite. Do not use HIGH_ORDER/MFH, attention or VQA loss.

methods.distinctness: k>1 independent factor products are pooled into each output coordinate; preserves MFB expansion/squeeze and normalization. Setting k=1 weakens distinction from MLB.
caveats: Omitting the source dropout is an explicit adaptation to the shared no-extra-dropout protocol.
Safe signed-square-root differs near zero from the ideal formula; record epsilon.
The small output width is not a reproduction of the source VQA model.

methods.title: MUTAN: Multimodal Tucker Fusion for Visual Question Answering
methods.paperEvidence: Sections3.1–3.3, Eq.(4)–(10): latent Tucker projections and rank-R slice factorization, giving a sum of second-stage projected products.

codeFiles.verified: First-stage linear_v/linear_q embeddings; R second-stage pairs in ModuleLists; sum of paired products.
Author-maintained successor, linked from original README: first projections then rank*mm_dim merge projections, reshape, sum across rank, final projection.

license.id: Original repo: NOT_FOUND; author successor: BSD-3-Clause
license.note: Do not assign the successor license retroactively to the original repository. New implementation follows the paper equations.

algorithm.formula: x=tanh(U0 L); y=tanh(V0 C); z=P(sum_{r=1..R} ((M_r x) elementwise_mul (N_r y)))
algorithm.dimensions: First-stage widths t_L=t_C=128; each second-stage factor maps128→128; R=4; P:128→128.
algorithm.pytorch_plan: Keep separate first-stage projections and nonlinearity; produce factor tensors[N,R,128], multiply and sum R. This expresses rank-constrained Tucker-core interaction.

methods.distinctness: Two-stage latent projections and rank-R per-output core slices. Without intermediate nonlinearity, composed linear maps can collapse algebraically toward direct MFB factorization; do not silently remove this stage.
caveats: The source permits optional nonlinearities; this candidate fixes first-stage tanh and no extra dropout.
R=4 and width128 are proposed resource-bounded settings, not the original paper hyperparameters.

methods.title: BLOCK: Bilinear Superdiagonal Fusion for Visual Question Answering and Visual Relationship Detection
methods.domain: Visual question answering and visual relationship detection
methods.paperEvidence: Section2, Eq.(3)–(5): block-term decomposition, independent interactions within projected chunks, concatenation and output projection; rank constraints can be placed on block slices.

codeFiles.verified: linear0/linear1 to mm_dim, get_chunks, per-chunk rank expansion, product reshape[batch,rank,chunk], rank sum, per-chunk signed-sqrt/L2, concatenate, linear_out.

algorithm.formula: x=U L,y=V C; split x,y into B chunks. q_b=sum_{r=1..R}(M_br x_b elementwise_mul N_br y_b); z=P(concat_b L2Normalize(signed_sqrt(q_b)))
algorithm.dimensions: mm_dim=128,B=4,chunk width32,R=4; each per-chunk factor maps32→128 then reshape[N,R,32]; concat128→output128.
algorithm.pytorch_plan: Preserve independent within-block modules and normalize each block before concatenation, following pos_norm=before_cat.

methods.distinctness: Block-restricted core trades cross-block interactions for several wider projected subspaces. Use B>1 and chunk width>1; a single block approaches MUTAN, scalar blocks approach CP/MLB.
caveats: This is the low-rank Block class, not its full-core BlockTucker alternative.
BLOCK and MUTAN are related tensor factorizations, not unrelated mechanisms.
Use stable signed-square-root near zero and record its numerical adaptation.

methods.title: Multimodal Compact Bilinear Pooling for Visual Question Answering and Visual Grounding
methods.domain: Visual question answering and visual grounding
methods.paperEvidence: Section3.1 and Algorithm1: fixed independent CountSketch hashes/signs and FFT convolution approximate an outer-product feature without materializing it.

codeFiles.verified: Invokes CompactBilinear with width16000, followed by SignedSqrt, L2Normalize and classifier.
Author README links this Caffe branch. Fixed random hashes/signs, signed hash accumulation, FFT, complex multiplication and inverse FFT are present.

license.id: BSD-2-Clause for VQA repo; separate UC Berkeley permission notice for CompactBilinear dependency
license.note: Do not flatten dependency terms into the VQA root license. Implement the mathematical sketch afresh in native torch.

algorithm.dimensions: Local/context tokens each128 after shared wrapper; independent CountSketch width1024; P:1024→128.
algorithm.pytorch_plan: Private seeded generator initializes independent hash/sign buffers once; serialize buffers in state_dict. Use scatter_add or equivalent signed accumulation and native rfft/irfft with explicit length1024. Keep float32 FFT and stabilized power transform.

methods.distinctness: Interaction sketch itself is fixed and randomized, unlike the five learned interaction mechanisms; only downstream projection and upstream encoders learn.
caveats: 1024 is a smaller sketch than the paper's common16000; collision/noise tradeoff is an adaptation, not equivalent source capacity.
Hash/sign buffers must not change per forward or disturb the run's global RNG.
MCB can add FFT overhead despite its compact output; no throughput claim is established.

methods.title: Bilinear Attention Networks
methods.domain: Visual question answering and phrase grounding
methods.paperEvidence: Section3 Eq.(5)–(10): bilinear attention across channel pairs and attention-weighted bilinear features. Eq.(11) describes optional multi-glimpse residual stacking.

codeFiles.verified: Low-rank bilinear logits over pairs via einsum; weighted einsum gives bilinear pooled feature.
Masks invalid visual tokens and softmaxes the flattened pair axis.
Full VQA model uses sequential residual glimpses and optional counting; these components are not copied into the restricted readout.

algorithm.formula: s_j=p^T(ReLU(U L) elementwise_mul ReLU(V E_j)); a=masked_softmax_j(s); z=P(sum_j a_j*(ReLU(Uv L) elementwise_mul ReLU(Vv E_j)))
algorithm.dimensions: Local query[N,1,128], evidence[N,4,128], rank128, one attention glimpse, pooled output[N,128].
algorithm.pytorch_plan: Use distinct learned score and value projections, mask inactive evidence logits, and apply explicit all-masked zero handling. Normalize only over four legal current readout evidence tokens.

methods.distinctness: Learns evidencewise pair scores and aggregates multiplicative values; the other five candidates use a fixed active-mean context vector before fusion.
caveats: One Local query is the single-query special case of BAN, not its full two-multichannel advantage; label BAN-inspired readout.
No tokenization of past trajectory, box counting, VQA classifier, new auxiliary loss, or multi-glimpse recurrence is included.
Zero-test masking in old source is replaced by authoritative explicit masks; this is necessary for legitimate zero features and inactive NaNs.

gaps: OpenReview/CVF endpoints were challenged or denied during this audit; the corresponding arXiv primary PDFs were read successfully.
Original MFB and original MUTAN repositories have no detected root license; precise successor/dependency licensing distinctions are recorded per method.
No source model was executed or reproduced; these six entries authorize only source-grounded readout adaptations and do not establish cfg84 effectiveness.
